```{r}
# Import packages
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
# import data
data <- read_csv("../data/megazord.csv")
```

When given the dataset, I saw lattitute and longitude, and my first instinct was to plot them to visualize where the birds all are.  
Later, when given the manuscript to read, it was cool to see that the neighbourhoods I plotted here align closely with the map presented in the manuscript.

```{r}
# Set data types and select input columns
data <- data %>% 
    mutate(across(contains("UST"), ~ as.factor(.x)), 
        does_it_match = as.factor(does_it_match),
        number_of_matches = as.integer(number_of_matches))
```

```{r}
# NOTE: This initial attempt at graphing locations to determine the central individual contained an error: 
# did not take into account the fact that there was more than one "M1" (one for each neighbourhood)
# Also latitude and longitude should be switched, as shown in later graphs
ggplot() +
    geom_path(data = data, aes(x = M1_Lat, y = M1_Lon, color="Male 1")) +
    geom_point(data = data, aes(x = M1_Lat, y = M1_Lon, color="Male 1")) +
    geom_path(data = data, aes(x = M2_Lat, y = M2_Lon, color="Male 2")) +
    geom_point(data = data, aes(x = M2_Lat, y = M2_Lon, color="Male 2")) +
    geom_path(data = data, aes(x = M3_Lat, y = M3_Lon, color="Male 3")) +
    geom_point(data = data, aes(x = M3_Lat, y = M3_Lon, color="Male 3")) +
    geom_path(data = data, aes(x = M4_Lat, y = M4_Lon, color="Male 4")) +
    geom_point(data = data, aes(x = M4_Lat, y = M4_Lon, color="Male 4")) +
    geom_path(data = data, aes(x = M5_Lat, y = M5_Lon, color="Male 5")) +
    geom_point(data = data, aes(x = M5_Lat, y = M5_Lon, color="Male 5")) +
    geom_path(data = data, aes(x = M6_Lat, y = M6_Lon, color="Male 6")) +
    geom_point(data = data, aes(x = M6_Lat, y = M6_Lon, color="Male 6")) +
    xlab("Latitude") +
    ylab("Longitude")
```

```{r}
# Flight paths, colour by individual

```

```{r}
# Flight paths, colour by neighbourhood (shape by individual, not shown in legend)
ggplot() +
    geom_path(data = data, aes(y = M1_Lat, x = M1_Lon, color = neighbourhood)) +
    geom_point(data = data, aes(y = M1_Lat, x = M1_Lon, color = neighbourhood), shape = 1) +
    geom_path(data = data, aes(y = M2_Lat, x = M2_Lon, color = neighbourhood)) +
    geom_point(data = data, aes(y = M2_Lat, x = M2_Lon, color = neighbourhood), shape = 2) +
    geom_path(data = data, aes(y = M3_Lat, x = M3_Lon, color = neighbourhood)) +
    geom_point(data = data, aes(y = M3_Lat, x = M3_Lon, color = neighbourhood), shape = 3) +
    geom_path(data = data, aes(y = M4_Lat, x = M4_Lon, color = neighbourhood)) +
    geom_point(data = data, aes(y = M4_Lat, x = M4_Lon, color = neighbourhood), shape = 4) +
    geom_path(data = data, aes(y = M5_Lat, x = M5_Lon, color = neighbourhood)) +
    geom_point(data = data, aes(y = M5_Lat, x = M5_Lon, color = neighbourhood), shape = 5) +
    geom_path(data = data, aes(y = M6_Lat, x = M6_Lon, color = neighbourhood)) +
    geom_point(data = data, aes(y = M6_Lat, x = M6_Lon, color = neighbourhood), shape = 6) +
    ylab("Latitude") +
    xlab("Longitude")
```

```{r}
# Now plotting the above graphs using for loops to keep code concise
# Flight paths, colour by neighbourhood (shape by individual, not shown in legend)
fig = ggplot()
for (i in 1:6) {
    fig <- fig + 
        geom_path(data = data, aes_string(y = sprintf("M%s_Lat", i), x = sprintf("M%s_Lon", i), color = "neighbourhood"), shape = i) +
        geom_point(data = data, aes_string(y = sprintf("M%s_Lat", i), x = sprintf("M%s_Lon", i), color = "neighbourhood"), shape = i)
}
# sprintf
```

```{r}
# Now plotting the above graphs using for loops to keep code concise
# Flight paths, colour by individual
fig = ggplot()
for (i in 1:6) {
    fig <- fig + 
        geom_path(data = data, aes(y = !!sym(sprintf("M%s_Lat", i)), x = !!sym(sprintf("M%s_Lon", i)), color = ID), shape = i) +
        geom_point(data = data, aes(y = !!sym(sprintf("M%s_Lat", i)), x = !!sym(sprintf("M%s_Lon", i)), color = ID), shape = i)
}
fig <- fig + geom_path(data = filter(data, neighbourhood=="centre"), aes(x="M2_Lon", y="M2_Lat", color='black'))
fig <- fig + geom_point(data = filter(data, neighbourhood=="centre"), aes(x="M2_Lon", y="M2_Lat", color='black'))
fig
```

```{r}
list_of_samples = list()
# For every individual bird and every song type
for (id in unique(data$ID)) {
	print(id)
	for (song_type in unique(data$UST)) {
		print(song_type)
		# Get 40 random rows
		sample <- slice_sample(filter(data, UST == song_type, ID == id), n=40)
        print(sample)
		# Add the sample to our list of samples
        list_of_samples <- append(list_of_samples, list(sample))
		# Or insert code here to do whatever you want to do with that sample (create a directory and store the files!?)
	}
}
```
